subject: Brighton Health VPC node-flap: required exec coordination and temporary fallback
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: olivia.gray@brightonhealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: (no subject) - sudden 5xx/latency spike this morning

Laura —

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency jump and intermittent 502s on our private VPC cluster this morning (around 08:40 PT). The impact is on our charting microservice that calls your inference endpoint for clinical summarization — experiments point to a small set of long requests causing hot KV cache misses.

Can your ops team advise immediate mitigations? We briefly toggled our prefetch to reduce request fanout but that only helped a little. We need a short-term fallback plan and an ETA for a root-cause remediation.

Attaching the error window CSV and a screenshot from our infra team.

— Sam

Attachments: brighton_q3_token_latency.csv (csv), grafana_node_spike_20261115.png (image)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightonhealth.com>, Olivia Gray <olivia.gray@brightonhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/latency spike this morning

Sam / Olivia —

Thanks for the data, Sam. Marcus is already on initial triage and I’ve looped in our infrastructure lead, Jonas, for kernel/path decisions. Quick plan for the next 24 hours:

- Marcus: run targeted KV cache warm-up and temporarily raise per-container token limit to reduce aborts (eta 30–60m).
- Jonas: validate whether a quantized model fallback (lower mem profile) can be routed for requests longer than 8k tokens to reduce tail latency (eta 2–3 hrs).
- I (customer lead): will coordinate a brief exec sync with Brighton to confirm the temporary fallback and any billing/credits ask.

Immediate ask for Brighton: if you can route a small percentage (~5%) of traffic to an async queue and provide the queue URL, we can offload the longest jobs while we stabilize.

I will keep you updated at the 60-minute mark.

— Laura

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden 5xx/latency spike this morning

Laura / team —

Triage summary (10:02):
- Root symptom: transient node "flapping" behavior where a small subset of workers hit an unexpected KV cache eviction pattern; those workers then returned slow responses and occasional 502s when they failed to rehydrate quickly.
- Likely trigger: recent qkv cache eviction threshold change in the private deploy (we shipped a micro-tune last night).

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Restored previous KV eviction threshold on the affected AZ; nodes have started to stabilize (p95 trending down but still elevated).
2) Increased per-container request timeout and enabled soft-fail routing to the standby lower-memory model (quantized-psi-4b) for requests > 6k tokens.
3) Kicked off a controlled drain/reboot of two suspect hosts to remove the bad kernel state (ETA 40m).

Next steps (action items):
- Jonas: run kernel parameter sanity checks and patch the host-level preemption settings (ETA 3–4h).
- Laura: coordinate exec-level communication with Brighton and confirm whether they want an SLA credit request submitted (Laura to confirm by EOD).
- Marcus: prepare a short postmortem draft and a short-term playbook (uploading playbook_v1.md to the shared drive).

I will post updated p95/p99 snapshots in 30 mins.

— Marcus

Attachments: temporary_fallback_playbook_v1.md (md)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightonhealth.com>, Olivia Gray <olivia.gray@brightonhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:44:00 -0800
Subject: Brighton Health — stabilization update and exec sync request

Sam / Olivia —

Quick update and ask from our side now that we've stabilized the immediate impact:

What we did (summary):
- Rolled back last night's KV eviction micro-tune in your AZ — that removed the core source of node rehydration failures.
- Deployed a temporary routing policy to send requests longer than 6k tokens to our quantized-psi-4b variant while we finish a thorough kernel-level patch.
- Drained and replaced two hosts that exhibited repeated OOM/eviction cycles.

What we need from Brighton:
1) Exec sync (30 minutes) tomorrow to agree on: whether to keep the quantized fallback as a persistent option, timing for the permanent kernel patch, and whether you want us to submit a credit for the downtime window. Marcus and Jonas will be on the call to walk through technical detail.
2) Confirmation if your team can try the async queue option for low-priority long jobs (we saw it cut queued tail latency by ~60% in early testing).

Proposed times: Tue 11/17 10:00 PT or Tue 11/17 15:00 PT — please confirm which works and who from your exec team will join.

We’ll attach the short postmortem and the mitigation playbook to the Drive link and open an INF ticket for the permanent kernel fix (linked).

Thanks again for the quick collaboration on this — I know these incidents are disruptive and we appreciate your patience.

— Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
